data.cultural_impact: Kamalnath is a name rooted in Hindu mythology and culture. The lotus flower is considered sacred in Hinduism, representing purity, beauty, and radiance. The name Kamalnath honors this reverence for the lotus and symbolizes success, wealth, and positivity.
data.spiritual_significance: In Hindu tradition, the god Vishnu is often depicted sitting or reclining on a lotus flower. Devotees of Vishnu honor Kamalnath as a spiritual connection to the divinity of the lotus and Vishnu himself. This name evokes the love, compassion, and creative power embodied by Vishnu and the lotus, inspiring a sense of devotion, self-reflection, and personal growth.
data.spiritual_symbolism: The name Kamalnath signifies the embodiment of lotus (Kamal) and Lord Shiva (Nath). It symbolizes the spiritual journey towards enlightenment, carried out with the grace and purity of a lotus flower.

vedic_reference.note: Not found in Vedas or Upanishads, but originates from Sanskrit.

historical_references.reference: Kamalnath was a renowned Jain Tirthankara of the 22nd cycle of the Jain Calendar. He is also known as Mahavira IV and is considered the 24th Jain Tirthankara. His teachings emphasized the attainment of Kevala Jnana or omniscience through personal experience. The time period for Kamalnath's life is estimated to be around 1000 BCE.

Kamalnath is also mentioned in various Hindu texts, particularly in the Puranas, as a powerful Shaivite deity. He is believed to be the guardian of Kailash, the abode of Lord Shiva. The exact time period for this belief is not mentioned in Hindu scriptures but it is believed to predate the Common Era.
